author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Burmese pythons are an invasive species in the Everglades, and the challenge is part of initiative to remove them

The winner of this year’s annual Florida Python Challenge hunted down and eliminated 96 invasive Burmese pythons from the Everglades national park, as part of an initiative to remove hundreds of the snakes from the area every year.

The challenge invites hunters to participate in 10 days of capturing and humanely euthanizing as many of the invasive snakes as possible across eight designated hunting locations, with the winner taking home a cash prize of $10,000. The event is hosted by Florida fish, wildlife and conservation (FWC), the south Florida water management district, the National Park Service and others.

Continue reading...
title: Winner of Florida python hunting contest nabs 96 snakes: ‘I was on a mission’

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Variety of prescriptions were found in blood of mother accused of strangling her three children, court hears

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

The trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of killing her three children in January 2023, continued on Wednesday with a forensic toxicologist testifying to the variety and concentration of medications found in the defendant’s blood.

Justin Brower, a forensic toxicologist with NMS Laboratories, testified that his lab examined the levels of four psychiatric medications detected in Clancy’s blood after she allegedly strangled her children and attempted to take her own life.
title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial: toxicologist testifies about medications found in defendant’s blood

description:
Chief executive Robert Thomson says ‘crass kleptomaniac’ AI companies are ‘in possession of stolen goods’

News Corp has reported a slight slide in digital subscriptions at its Australian mastheads, erasing recent gains, among otherwise robust financials at the Rupert Murdoch-backed global conglomerate.

Digital subscribers at News Corp Australia – a division that includes the Australian, the Daily Telegr
title: News Corp subscriptions fall in Australia as company takes aim at ‘slimy’ AI slop

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo and agency
description:
Jeanine John Taele detained for ‘suspicious’ behavior and charged with possession of unregistered short-barreled rifle

A California man who was arrested at Donald Trump’s Los Angeles-area golf course ahead of a presidential visit is facing more charges, as authorities released new details about the investigation.

Authorities say federal agents first observed 38-year-old Jeanine John Taele near the golf grounds in Rancho Palos Verdes on 31 July, wearing an earpiece and capturing photographs and videos of security agents assessing the property.

Continue reading...
title: Man arrested at Trump’s California golf course faces more charges

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Husic to take ‘short’ period of leave after collision on Sydney motorway on Tuesday

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor MP Ed Husic was hospitalised this week after his car was involved in an accident with a truck travelling on Sydney’s M7 motorway.

The incident happened when the Chifley MP was travelling home from his electorate office, around 6.20pm on Tuesday, according to a spokesperson.
title: Labor MP Ed Husic taken to hospital with fractures and concussion after car accident

author: Nick Visser
description:
Police allege man issued threats on social media to find woman and hurt her. Follow today’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

News Corp’s Australian division weighs on robust results

News Corp has delivered a strong rise in revenue across its global business, despite weakness in its news division, marked by a slide in digital subscribers at its Australian mastheads.

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: NSW man charged over alleged threats of violence against female MP

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Changes come after report says Trump unhappy with helipad’s appearance and lawn’s slope

The White House has confirmed that contractors are redoing a new helipad built on the South Lawn to accommodate a new supersized Marine One chopper recently added to the presidential transport fleet.

A White House official said the changes to the circular concrete landing pad were ordered as “we continue to make improvements as part of the ongoing project to best match the needs of the White House”.

Continue reading...
title: White House confirms new helipad for supersized Marine One helicopter

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
President has sued the broadcaster for $10bn, claiming a documentary on 2021 Capitol attack led to financial harm

Donald Trump’s legal team is making an 11th-hour attempt to block a court order that would grant the BBC access to the president’s financial records, as part of his multibillion-dollar lawsuit against the British broadcaster.

Trump claims that the BBC’s 2024 documentary on the January 6 attacks have damaged the president’s business interests. In July, a Miami-based judge ruled that the president would have to start handing over detailed financial records to the BBC by 6 August. The records would reveal details into the hundreds of businesses owned by the US president’s family trust.

Continue reading...
title: Trump team pushes to block court order giving BBC access to financial records

author: Associated Press
description:
Murdaugh, whose murder convictions were overturned due to clerk’s misconduct, will face trial again

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A US federal judge has thrown out a lawsuit by Alex Murdaugh seeking $600,000 in legal fees from the former court clerk whose misconduct led to his murder convictions being overturned on appeal.

Murdaugh sued Becky Hill in May, saying she violated his right to a fair trial over the deaths of his wife and son.

Continue reading...
title: Judge tosses Alex Murdaugh’s $600,000 suit against former court clerk

author: George Chidi
description:
Thomas Smith, whose name remained on ballot, beats Republican rivals in primary contest for eighth district

Thomas Smith withdrew from the Republican primary contest for Michigan’s eighth district last month. On Tuesday, he won the nomination.

Unofficial results show Smith with more than 50% of the vote, according to the Associated Press, defeating the man he endorsed, anti-abortion activist Al Lemmo, and the man Donald Trump endorsed, former federal law enforcement officer Amir Hassan.

Continue reading...
title: Republican who withdrew last month beats Trump-backed rival in Michigan

author: Jessica Elgot, Alexandra Topping and Fiona Harvey
description:
Health secretary says global heating means UK hospitals and GPs will have to prepare for summer as well as winter peaks of demand

Adapting to global heating: which UK public services are struggling in hot weather?

The NHS has been warned to prepare for potential annual summer crises caused by extreme heat with the same pressures as winter, as heatwaves caused by the climate crisis become routine in the UK.

The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said NHS staff were feeling A&E pressures that would normally be expected only during flu season – and said the government would use major investment in NHS infrastructure to tackle the health service’s resilience to high summer temperatures.

Continue reading...
title: NHS must prepare for annual summer heat pressures, says Yvette Cooper

author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
description:
As NHS told to prepare for extreme weather, strain also felt in other areas including transport and farming

NHS must prepare for annual summer heat pressures, says Yvette Cooper

The NHS has been told it must become more resilient to increasingly frequent heatwaves supercharged by the climate crisis, as the UK government puts adaptation to extreme heat high on its agenda. But what other public services are already feeling the strain?

Continue reading...
title: Adapting to global heating: which UK public services are struggling in hot weather?

author: Geraldine McKelvie
description:
Thames Valley chief says he may join Police Federation in court if Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers are freed from prison

The chief constable of Thames Valley police has said he will consider joining legal action against the government if it fails to block the early release of two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers.

The Police Federation is contemplating going to court in its attempts to keep Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers in prison.

Continue reading...
title: Threat of legal action if PC Andrew Harper’s killers are released early

author: Richard Adams
description:
University says it has ‘new information’ about academic career of Jason Arday, the youngest black professor in its history

Jason Arday, the Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism and embellishment, is to face investigation by the university after it said it received “new information” about his qualifications and career.

Cambridge initially defended Arday – the youngest black professor appointed in the university’s history, with a compelling life story of educational disadvantage – as “the victim of a vile campaign”. But as questions mounted over Arday’s own claims, the university’s leaders felt that Cambridge’s reputation was in danger.

Continue reading...
title: Cambridge announces investigation into professor accused of plagiarism

author: Reuters
description:
Joint statement is being finalised, but Tehran says deal alone would not guarantee waterway’s security

  • Middle East crisis live – latest updates

Iran and Oman have reached an understanding on ⁠the geographic coordinates for a shipping route through the strait of Hormuz, and ⁠a joint announcement ⁠is ​being finalised, provided certain third parties did not interfere, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil ⁠Baghaei said on Wednesday.

Baghaei added that any such agreement between Iran and Oman would not, by ⁠itself, guarantee security in the strategic waterway.

Continue reading...
title: Iran and Oman reach understanding on coordinates of route through Hormuz, Iran ministry says

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
MTA to sell remaining machines – which weigh up to 1,050lbs – as it transitions to contactless fare system

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) of New York City has begun auctioning off its final MetroCard vending machines, offering New Yorkers the chance to own one of the transit system’s most recognizable fixtures as the agency continues its transition to Omny.

The auction opened on Wednesday morning and will run through 19 August, according to the MTA. The agency is offering a limited number of retired MetroCard Vending Machines (MVM) and MetroCard Express Machines (MEM), which have served subway riders for decades.

Continue reading...
title: New York City transit auctions off last MetroCard machines: ‘Wild home decor idea’

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Democrats ‘united by a common purpose: putting a check on Trump’, Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand say

  • Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate primary

  • What we learned from midterm primary elections

Leading Democrats quickly papered over whatever qualms they had about progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed after his win in the Michigan Senate primary was confirmed on Wednesday, instead welcoming the former public health official as their champion against the Republican nominee, Mike Rogers.

The state is now key to Democrats’s hopes of retaking control of the chamber in November’s midterm elections. Winning in Michigan
title: Top Democrats set aside qualms and embrace progressive Abdul El-Sayed

author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
description:
Initial evidence suggests the drone, which was found near Ukrainian cargo planes at the German airport, came from Russia

The armed drone found at Leipzig airport on Wednesday may not have exploded, but the fact that it got inside the perimeter, close to Ukrainian cargo planes, raises obvious concerns for the security of international aviation.

Though the identity of the culprits is unknown, the initial evidence points firmly towards a Russian-orchestrated plot. It is the first time that a drone with explosives has been found in Europe far from the Ukrainian border.

Continue reading...
title: The Leipzig drone bomb marks a dangerous escalation for Europe

author: Oscar Lopez in Mexico City
description:
César Gastélum was filming outside a fast-food outlet in Sinaloa state when he was killed by a motorbike driver

A popular Mexican influencer has been shot dead while doing a live stream on social media outside a restaurant in Sinaloa state, where lethal cartel violence has become widespread.

César Gastélum, who had nearly 600,000 followers on TikTok and was known for making comedy videos, was filming with two friends outside a fast-food restaurant in the city of Culiacán. The three were dressed in the bright orange jackets and backpacks of food delivery drivers.

Continue reading...
title: Mexican influencer shot dead while streaming live on social media

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Aaron Farinacci is accused of starting the Old Trails fire that has destroyed homes and forced thousands to flee

The Washington state man accused of starting a wildfire that has destroyed homes and forced thousands to flee around Spokane was previously questioned in connection with two fire investigations last year, according to court documents.

Authorities allege that Aaron Farinacci, 37, of Spokane, started Old Trails fire, one of three major wildfires burning in Spokane county in north-eastern Washington. He was arrested on Monday and booked on suspicion of first-degree arson.

The Associated Press contributed reporting

Continue reading...
title: Suspect in Washington state wildfire was questioned about blazes last year

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
The president is constantly assigning motives, identifying heroes and villains, and telling his audience what to think

  • This was originally published in This Week in Trumpland. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday

From Charles Barkley to Thierry Henry to John McEnroe, the path from the arena to the commentary box is well trodden, and plenty of politicians have made the transition from elected office to the TV studio. One man, however, insists on doing both at the same time.

Donald Trump is the US pre
title: Trump is pioneering the role of commentator-in-chief when issues grow thorny

description:
Joanna Whaley, ex-megachurch pastor who endured years of conversion practices, comfortably bested her opponents

  • US politics live – latest updates

A former megachurch pastor who endured 15 years of conversion practices is set to become the first transgender member of Michigan’s state legislature after winning a Democratic primary election on Tuesday.

Joanna Whale
title: Michigan nominates first trans woman for state legislature

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Filing by attorney general Raúl Torrez comes after DoJ appears to have ignored deadline for key Epstein ranch files

New Mexico filed a lawsuit against the US Department of Justice and acting attorney general, Todd Blanche, on Wednesday for “stonewalling” its criminal investigation into the activities of the late financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein at a remote ranch in the state.

Raúl Torrez, the New Mexico attorney general, had said he was mulling the possibility of legal action if the justice department did not share with him by 31 July information about the alleged historical abuse of girls and young women at Epstein’s Zorro ranch about 30 miles south of Santa Fe.

Continue reading...
title: New Mexico sues justice department for ‘stonewalling’ Epstein investigation

author: Dharna Noor
description:
Activist who rallied around a datacenter moratorium will face incumbent Republican Tom Barrett in November

  • US politics live – latest updates

William Lawrence, a prominent environmental organizer who foregrounded his support for a datacenter moratorium, has won the Democratic primary in Michigan’s seventh congressional district in a victory for progressives.

Lawrence was a co-founder of the youth-led climate justice organization the Sunrise Movement, the group that in 2018 mainstreamed calls for a Green New Deal to battle economic injustice while rapidly phasing out planet-warming fossil fuels. The 36-year-old defeated Bridget Brink, a former US a
title: Progressive climate organizer William Lawrence wins Michigan Democratic House primary

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
New data shows the federal government scheme has been used by high-income borrowers, including one couple earning an annual $674,000

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The government’s 5% deposit scheme for first home buyers has enabled the purchase of nearly 1,500 properties that were turned into investments, new data shows.

The scheme is also helping hundreds of Australians earning more than $300,000 a year, after Labor stopped excluding high-income borrowers.

Continue reading...
title: Nearly 1,500 properties bought using Australia’s first home buyers' 5% deposit scheme converted into investments

author: Catie McLeod and Jonathan Barrett
description:
Add-on fees such as the new overhead locker baggage charge can make it harder to compare air fares, experts say

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Cut-price fares may now be merely a facade for seemingly endless add-on fees after Jetstar’s new carry-on luggage charge meant the airline joined a growing number monetising basic services in the sky.

The new structure, announced by Qantas’s low-cost carrier on Wednesday, will mean from next year tickets will only include one “under seat bag”, such as a backpack, handbag or laptop bag.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Just an easy cash grab’: why Jetstar is charging customers for carry-on luggage

author: Vivian Ho
description:
Police arrested a woman in central London after four men were found with stab wounds in the shopping and entertainment district

Matt Bishop, 42, who works at a consultancy firm just next to scene, told the Press Association that the woman arrested appeared “quite old” and had short hair.

“She didn’t seem to be particularly coherent. She was pretty incoherent in what she was shouting. The officer was asking what language she was shouting,” he said.

Continue reading...
title: Woman arrested after four men stabbed in Covent Garden – latest

author: Associated Press
description:
Scientists at a biotech company have used gene editing to create two hypoallergenic beagles that don't trigger allergies

Matt Walker couldn’t pet a dog without sneezing – until he and other scientists used a gene editing technique to produce a hypoallergenic beagle named Bailey.

Now, he can feed Bailey spoons of peanut butter while she lies on his lap and play fetch with her in Central Park. His allergies didn’t go away: Bailey’s saliva and hair no longer contain a key allergy-causing protein.

Continue reading...
title: Gene-edited beagles may offer a future option for people with dog allergies

author: Alexandra Villarreal in New York
description:
Federal lawsuit alleges kids are being repatriated despite many of them qualifying to remain in the US legally

The Trump administration is deliberately targeting children who came to the US unaccompanied by a parent or guardian as it pushes to quickly return them to the countries they fled – amid “drastic policy changes” in immigration courts, according to allegations in a federal lawsuit shared with the Guardian.

The plaintiffs in the lawsuit are trying to prevent imminent deportation to the places from where they escaped danger or harm.

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration targets children amid push to ‘deport at all costs’

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Men allegedly used exotic animals for photoshoots featuring a ring of fire in a parking garage in Maryland

Two Baltimore, Maryland, men are facing charges for allegedly using exotic animals – including snakes, a lemur and a spider monkey – in photoshoots featuring three semi-clothed models and a ring of fire in a garage beneath a luxury shopping complex.

Photographer Vernon Crowfey III, the 32-year-old owner of the company Photogeniks, was arrested in Towson, Maryland, on 16 July after an undercover officer arranged a shoot with the animals.

Continue reading...
title: Two US men charged for allegedly using snakes, a lemur and a monkey for exotic photoshoots

author: Richard Luscombe and agencies
description:
Controllers allegedly failed to halt flights, leading to a ‘loss of separation’ with a departing passenger jet

An air “safety incident” in which Donald Trump’s Marine One helicopter came closer than permitted to another aircraft over Washington DC is under investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

Air traffic controllers are believed to have mistakenly failed to halt commercial flights at Ronald Reagan national airport in northern Virginia on Tuesday afternoon when the military helicopter lifted off from the White House with the president on board.

Continue reading...
title: FAA investigates air ‘safety incident’ involving Trump’s Marine One

author: Guardian staff
description:
Congressional ethics panel had recommended Edwards face censure over its findings on ‘hostile work environment’

  • US politics live – latest updates

Chuck Edwards announced he would not run for re-election after the US House of Representatives ethics committee determined the US congressman “fostered a hostile work environment and engaged in sexual harassment” by giving gifts and lavishing attention on two young female staffers.

Edwards, a Republican for North Carolina, said he would complete his current term, which is due to end in January.

Continue reading...
title: Republican Chuck Edwards drops bid for re-election after report finding sexual harassment of staffers

author: Pjotr Sauer
description:
Assassination attempt demonstrates Ukraine’s ability to continue clandestine operations deep inside Russian territory

  • Europe live – latest updates

The head of a leading Russian drone manufacturer has been critically injured in a car bomb near Ekaterinburg, in what appears to be the latest in a series of assassination attempts targeting figures linked to the country’s war in Ukraine.

Vladimir Tkachuk, the founder of the private drone manufacturer Uraldronzavod, was rushed to intensive care on Wednesday after a bomb planted beneath his Mercedes exploded, according to Russian state media, citing emergency services. His bodyguard was killed in the explosion.
title: Head of drone manufacturer critically injured in car bomb in Russia

author: Martin Belam
description:
Haley Stevens trails progressive in Senate primary as counting continues. Plus, meet the man who names cockroaches after Tolkein and Pokémon characters

Good morning.

A Democratic Senate primary in Michigan remains too close to call, with Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive former public health official, holding a narrow lead over the establishment-backed congresswoman Haley Stevens. The battleground state is crucial to the party’s hopes of winning back control of the Senate in November.

Who won in the crowded primary in Washington state? The Democratic representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez secured one of two spots in the all-party primary, overcoming criticism from both the left and the right. She will face t
title: Michigan Democratic race to close to call with El-Sayed in narrow lead | First Thing

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Union exploring options to oppose program that would put US airport screening into hands of private contractors

The labor union representing workers at the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) is raising alarms over a new program that will expand privatizing security checkpoints at three airports.

The agency informed the union last month of plans to enact the TSA Gold+ program, which would shift security and control of the screening technology into the hands of private contractors at airports in Tampa, Charleston and Des Moines. Union workers are expected to lose their union contract and benefits once a contractor takes over.

Continue reading...
title: ‘They’re selling the safety of the traveling public’: TSA workers decry Trump privatization push

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Jake Richard acknowledges ‘unimaginable pain’ of Harper’s family but says government faces an ‘unenviable position’

Good morning and welcome to the UK politics blog.

Ministers continue to defend the release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers as part of the government’s early prisoner release scheme, despite a potential legal challenge from the Police Federation.

Well, look, we understand that people are angry. The Harper family are, of course, angry. The police are angry too.

We’re angry that we’re in this situation where we face the unenviable position of having to make sure that we have a sustainable prison system, which is so vital to a functioning law and order system in our country, but also that we do right by victims as far as possible.

Because without a functioning prison system, it means it’s difficult for police to make arrests, it’s difficult for our courts to try cases, and it could mean to the collapse of law and order in this
title: Justice minister defends early release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers amid possible legal challenge – UK politics live

author: Josh Butler
description:
Energy minister says Australian households and energy reliability will be protected by new federal legislation

Energy minister Chris Bowen says the federal government will override state governments that oppose new national rules on datacentres, with commonwealth legislation forcing new AI datacentres to be powered by renewable energy and banning those fuelled by gas.

Bowen said he expected his counterparts in Queensland and the Northern Territory – who had protested the new federal rules at a meeting last week – to be unhappy with the move, but said the Albanese government was committed to powering the AI revolution with renewable energy.

Continue reading...
title: Chris Bowen vows to override Queensland and NT to force renewables-powered AI datacentres

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Sarah Henderson says bill ignores gambling inducements, uniting parties and independents against controversial legislation

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor will be forced to make major changes to its planned crackdown on online gambling advertising, as the Coalition, Greens and independents demand tougher rules to stop betting companies offering generous inducements as well as further limits on broadcast ads.

After a two-day inquiry including sensational evidence that gamblin
title: Labor’s gambling reform friendless as Coalition withholds support amid drug and sex worker allegations

author: Yvonne C Lam
description:
In a Choice test of 48 products, the Aldi powder also came out on top for top loaders

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Consumer advocacy group Choice has put more than 40 supermarket laundry detergent products through the wringer, naming two Omo and one Aldi product as its best performers – while some other brands perform barely better than water.

In a lab test of 48 laundry powders, liquids and capsules, Aldi Trimat Advanced Laundry Powder Concentrate, Omo Active Clean Powder and Omo Ultimate Powder shared equal-first billing for front loader washing machines, with all three products scoring 82% overall
title: Test for Australia’s best laundry detergent sees Aldi and Omo tied for first place

author: Hettie O'Brien
description:
In today’s newsletter: The past week shows how quickly images, rumours and ​right-wing political opportunism can eclipse the facts on the ground

Good morning. Last week, an estimated 72,000 migrants began crossing into a tiny Spanish enclave on the tip of Morocco. Within 24 hours, most of them had headed home. At least 88 people died after attempting the crossing, according to local officials. This isn’t the whole story of what happened over the last week, but the facts are worth remembering.

At an emergency meeting yesterday, EU interior ministers sought to draw a line under Ceuta, insisting that the passport-free Schengen area had never been at risk from the arrival of migrants at this scale. Despite this, much of the media coverage has suggested that events in Ceuta represent a territorial threat to Europe, sparking calls for greater security across the region’s bor
title: Wednesday briefing: ​How misinformation and ​a​ hardened immigration policy ​turned Ceuta ​into Europe’s ​latest ​flashpoint

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Kellie Sloane says ‘leaking a report is never good’ as Reformer Jean-Claude Perrottet tells inquiry group signed up members to ‘dodgy’ branches

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The younger brother of a former Liberal premier has told an anti-corruption watchdog that a group of young conservative power breakers, now under investigation for soliciting illegal donations, recruited members to “dodgy” branches controlled by rival factions.

Jean-Claude Perrottet, the younger brother of e
title: NSW Liberal leader defers decision on frontbencher Damien Tudehope after leak revelations at Icac

author: Lauren Gambino
description:
Two-term Democrat faced attacks from the left and right while defending a House seat in a territory Trump won

The Democratic representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez secured one of two spots in the state of Washington’s crowded, all-party primary, overcoming criticism from both the left and the right to advance in one of November’s most closely watched US congressional races.

The two-term Democrat – known for bucking her party on key issues – heads into the general election as she seeks to defend a district carried by Donald Trump in 2024 and a district that remains central to the battle for control of the House of Representatives. She will face the Republican state senator John Braun in November.

Continue reading...
title: Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez survives Washington’s crowded primary

author: Eva Corlett in Wellington
description:
Snow falls in Wellington for the first time in 15 years while snow blanketed Dunedin and Christchurch on the country’s south island

Temperatures have plummeted across New Zealand as an Antarctic cold snap hovers over the country, delighting the capital, Wellington, which experienced snow for the first time in 15 years, while giving a southern city’s residents a chance to ski through the streets.

The front moved in on Tuesday, with much of the country waking to freezing conditions, frosts, snowfall, hail and bitingly cold wind.

Continue reading...
title: New Zealand capital delights in rare snowfall as southern city residents ski down world’s steepest street

author: Josh Butler and Benita Kolovos
description:
Exclusive: Warren Pickering told 2025 podcast mass deportations ‘not a reality’ in Australia and suggested politicians over 55 should ‘handball it to the next generation’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation’s Victorian leader has previously said mass deportations in Australia are “not a reality” and “won’t happen”, in newly unearthed comments which raise further questions about Pauline Hanson’s signature policy to deport 75,000 people she says have overstayed vis
title: ‘Won’t happen’: One Nation Victoria leader’s comments raise questions about Hanson’s mass deportations policy

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
As home affairs minister’s National Press Club address is postponed, refugee advocates lament missed ‘opportunity to bring Australians together’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor will introduce new rules to cut net overseas migration and push temporary residents to leave Australia, despite a major speech on the subject by the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, being delayed.

But government sources told Guardian Australia the policy changes would not push net overseas migration
title: Labor plans migration cuts as Tony Burke pulls out of major speech

author: Chris Stein
description:
Wesley Bell wins in St Louis rematch dominated by Israel-Palestine issue

US politics live – latest updates

The Democratic congressman Wesley Bell won his primary in the St Louis area on Tuesday, ending the progressive former representative Cori Bush’s bid for a comeback and blunting the momentum pro-Palestinian candidates have shown in recent elections.

Bell unseated Bush, a democratic socialist who opposes aid to the US ally and accuses it of committing a genocide in Gaza, in the Democratic congressional primary two years ago with the help of millions of dollars in spending from pro-Israel groups. Their rematch this year came amid a spate of primary defeats of Democratic incumbents at the hands of progressive outsiders.
title: Wesley Bell wins Missouri House primary as Cori Bush comeback bid fails

author: Associated Press
description:
Missouri’s top election official has rejected a petition for a referendum on new congressional districts

Missouri’s top election official has rejected a citizens’ petition seeking a statewide referendum on the state’s redistricting plan backed by Donald Trump.

Supporters of the referendum had submitted hundreds of thousands of petition signatures in an effort to force a November election on whether to use a new US House map approved by the Republican-led state legislature. But the Republican secretary of state, Denny Hoskins, asserted on Tuesday that the petition was void because congressional redistricting plans cannot be subject to voter referendums.

Continue reading...
title: Missouri rejects citizens’ bid for vote on Trump-backed redistricting plan

author: David Smith Washington bureau chief
description:
Move is retaliation for Lula’s government refusal to approve Trump’s nominee for ambassador in Brasília

Donald Trump’s administration has revoked the visa of Brazil’s ambassador to the US in a sharp escalation of a diplomatic feud with the country’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

The US state department said Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti’s visa had been cancelled in retaliation for Brazil’s refusal to approve Trump’s nominee for ambassador in Brasília and its decision last month to deny visas to two US diplomats seeking to visit ahead of an October election.

Continue reading...
title: US revokes Brazil ambassador’s visa in escalation of diplomatic feud

author: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Assessment of more than 2,000 native species warns nearly one in five at high risk of deadly H5N1, including parrots, fur seals and quolls

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Almost 400 native Australian bird and mammal species have been assessed as being at a high risk – or worse – from the deadly H5N1 bird flu virus, a federal government assessment has revealed.

Some of Australia’s most beloved animals – including species of penguins, fur seals, quolls, dolphins, more than 300 birds and the Tasmanian devi
title: Penguins and dolphins among nearly 400 Australian species under threat from bird flu as ‘true extent of disaster’ revealed

author: Abené Clayton
description:
Trump loyalist, who also has president’s endorsement, has spent millions trying to prove 2020 election was ‘stolen’

Mike Lindell is leaving his role with the MyPillow company to focus on his campaign to become the next governor of Minnesota. In a social media post published on Tuesday, Lindell said that the company was strong enough to withstand his departure.

“This decision is not about walking away. It is about stepping forward to serve. I am putting Minnesota above myself, my title, and my business interests so I can give this campaign and the people of our state my full time, energy, and attention,” Lindell said.

Continue reading...
title: Mike Lindell, MyPillow CEO, steps down from post to run for Minnesota governor

author: Reuters
description:
Company and subsidiary Statsig alleged by US justice department to have favored foreign workers in hiring

OpenAI and a subsidiary will pay $3.2m to settle US government claims that they ⁠favored foreign workers with temporary employment visas and discriminated against US job applicants in recruiting and hiring, the justice department said ⁠on Tuesday.

The justice ⁠department in ​a release said that OpenAI and Statsig, which makes product development software, recruited foreign workers for some open positions and ⁠took various steps to discourage US workers from applying.

title: OpenAI pays $3.2m to settle claims it discriminated against US workers

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Anti-corruption watchdog’s long-awaited report finds ‘serious and concerning’ conduct by senior government members in dealings with union boss

Senior members of the former Daniel Andrews government engaged in “serious and concerning” conduct in their dealings with firefighters union boss Peter Marshall, a long-awaited report by the Victoria’s anti-corruption watchdog has found.

The report by the Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission (Ibac) was tabled in parliament on Wednesday, some eight years after their investigation first began.

title: Daniel Andrews’ government engaged in ‘concerning’ conduct but no evidence of firefighter union blackmail: Ibac report
